The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.)No.181/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thalassery is the appellant herein.
The 2 nd respondents in the O.P. is the respondent herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

According to the petitioner, on 28.11.2011 at about 8.10. a.m., while he was walking through the side of Mowancherry road, a car bearing registration No.KL-58B-5389 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner and in over speed came from the opposite side, hit him and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner cum driver and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the car.
3. The 1st respondents remained ex-parte.

The 2nd respondent/insurer filed a written statement,
admitting the policy and denying the negligence on the part of the 1st respondent.
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A7, and C1.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.9,30,500/-.
5. Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

6. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
7.

Heard Sri.K.N Abhilash, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri. P.G. Ganappan,
learned Standing Counsel for the 2 nd respondent.
8. The Point: The petitioner was aged 34 years on the date of the accident on 28.11.2011.
According to him, he was working as a Cleaner in a school bus getting a salary of Rs.6,000/- per month.
Petitioner has produced Exhibit A6 certificate issued from a school.
However, nobody was examined to prove Exhibit A6.

Therefore, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, 2025:KER:3247 Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Biju K.P vs The Branch Manager, M/S.National ...

In the instant case, the petitioner sustained grievous head injury, paralysed right side, lacerated wound over the chin, cheek, and loss of two teeth.
He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 80 days.
The petitioner produced Exhibit C1 disability certificate.
The medical board assessed his permanent physical disability at 50% and it was accepted as such by the Tribunal, while assessing the loss of disability.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that even now, the petitioner is suffering from the injuries sustained in the accident and hence he is unable to do any work or earn anything.
Therefore, he prayed for fixing the functional disability of the petitioner at 100%.
He has also produced the petitioner before the court for assessing the present condition.
10. The petitioner appeared in a wheelchair along with his wife.
He finds it difficult to stand or to walk without the support of a walking stick (even after 13 years).
He could not speak without difficulty and could not raise his right hand as it is paralysed.
He submitted that he requires the help of somebody else for his daily necessities.
On examination of the petitioner, 2025:KER:3247 I am satisfied that he is unable to carry on his job as a Cleaner or any other job or to earn any income of his own.

In the above circumstances, his functional disability is liable to be fixed 100%.
11.

Since on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 34, 40% of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.21,50,400/-.
12. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.75,000/- alone.

Towards bystander expenses, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,14,500/- and towards loss of amenities,
a sum of Rs.25,000/- was awarded.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the above heads are too meager when compared to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability suffered by him.

Since it is revealed that the petitioner is even now unable to do any work or earn anything and his functional disability is found to be 100%, compensation on the heads pain and suffering and loss of amenities are on the lesser side and therefore, compensation towards pain and suffering is 2025:KER:3247 enhanced to Rs.5,00,000/- and compensation for loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.2,50,000/-.
13. Since it is revealed that the petitioner requires the help of a bystander, through out his life, he is entitled to get the expense of a bystander.

In the decision in Kajal v. Jagadish Chand and Others, [
(2020) 4 SCC 413] for a minor in vegetative stage, the expense of two bystanders at the rate of Rs.5,000/- each with a multiplier of 18 was awarded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, I hold that the expense of one bystander will be sufficient to comply the requirement.

Since the multiplier to be applied in this case is 16, I hold that towards bystander's expense, the petitioner is entitled to get a sum at the rate of Rs.5,000/- for 16 years ie., Rs.9,60,000/- (5000x16x12).
14. Towards extra nourishment, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-, which is also on lesser side.

Considering the facts, the compensation towards extra nourishment is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-

Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.39,62,400/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
Sl. Head of claim Amount awarded The amount given No. by the Tribunal (Rs) in appeal (Rs.)

1 Loss of earning 36,000/- Nil 2 Transport to hospital 50,000/-
50,000/- 3 Extra nourishment 25,000/- 50,000/- 4 Damage to clothing and articles 2,000/- 2,000/- 5
Medical/bystanders expenses 1,41,500/- 9,60,000/- 6 Pain and suffering 75,000/- 5,00,000/- 7
Permanent disability 5,76,000/- 21,50,400/- 8 Loss of amenities 25,000/- 2,50,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the respondent/insurer is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.39,62,400/-/- (Rupees Thirty Nine Lakhs Sixty Two Thousand and Four Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Rate of interest for the enhanced compensation is limited to 8%).
18. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 2025:KER:3247 the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
